scene_1_arrival_at_the_eco_park.speaker: Rose
scene_1_arrival_at_the_eco_park.text: hara do mangrove , bukon eang it para sa bisita kundi para protektahan.
scene_1_arrival_at_the_eco_park.translation: This is the mangrove eco-park. It’s not just for visitors, but truly for conservation.

scene_1_arrival_at_the_eco_park.speaker: Player
scene_1_arrival_at_the_eco_park.text: It looks peaceful. I didn’t expect it to be this wide.

scene_1_arrival_at_the_eco_park.speaker: Manong Ambo
scene_1_arrival_at_the_eco_park.text: Mayad-ayad nga [DayPart] , mga bisita. iya kamo para makita do aton nga mangroves?
scene_1_arrival_at_the_eco_park.translation: [GoodDay], visitors. Are you here to see our coast and mangroves?

scene_1_arrival_at_the_eco_park.speaker: Rose
scene_1_arrival_at_the_eco_park.text: Yes, Manong Ambo. He’s the caretaker here.

scene_2_learning_about_mangroves.speaker: Manong Ambo
scene_2_learning_about_mangroves.text: ro mga ugat ru gakapyot sa eugta. kaya indi masamad bisan it bagyo.
scene_2_learning_about_mangroves.translation: The roots hold the soil. It won’t collapse even during storms.

scene_2_learning_about_mangroves.speaker: Manong Ambo
scene_2_learning_about_mangroves.text: hara gid. Kung uwa ra, ro baeas ag tubi hay magatao it kaeainan
scene_2_learning_about_mangroves.translation: Exactly. Without this, the sand and water would cause danger.

scene_2_learning_about_mangroves.speaker: Rose
scene_2_learning_about_mangroves.text: That’s why they say mangroves are natural shields.

scene_3_fishing_lesson.speaker: Manong Ambo
scene_3_fishing_lesson.text: Gusto ninyo magkantoguhan magpamunit? bukon eang para sa isda, kundi para sa pagtuon.
scene_3_fishing_lesson.translation: Do you want to try fishing? Not just for fish, but for learning.

choices.label: Yes, I want to learn how.
Maybe later, I just want to watch first.
I’m not really into fishing, sorry.

scene_3_fishing_lesson.speaker: Rose
scene_3_fishing_lesson.text: You’ll miss out. It’s part of the experience, balikbayan.

scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_nature.speaker: Rose
scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_nature.text: Tan-awa ru baybay — that’s “shore.” Tubi — water. eugta — soil. Baeas — sand.

scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_nature.speaker: Rose
scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_nature.text: Maisog — brave. Maeuya — weak. Malimpyo — clean. Mahigko — dirty.

scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_nature.speaker: Rose
scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_nature.text: tikang pa — keep walking. Pamati — listen. Pamunit — to fish. Tanom — plant.

scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_nature.speaker: Player
scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_nature.text: Okay, so pamunit is what Manong Ambo said earlier.

scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_nature.speaker: Rose
scene_4_vocabulary_practice_round_nature.text: Correct. And tanom — you’ll hear that a lot here, since mangroves are plants.

scene_5_reflection.speaker: Lola Jonabel
scene_5_reflection.text: maabo aton nga natun-an makarang adlaw. bukon eang it mga haeambaeun, kundi pati kultura man.
scene_5_reflection.translation: We learned so much today. Not just words, but culture too.

scene_5_reflection.speaker: Papa Jobert
scene_5_reflection.text: True. This place reminds me of my childhood.

scene_5_reflection.speaker: Rose
scene_5_reflection.text: And now it’s part of yours, balikbayan.
